mainTopic: How long a daughter is supported from her father's estate: the ארוסה, and questions about a ממאנת, a יבמה's daughter, and a שניה's daughter
overview: This amud opens with the end of an earlier discussion: a reported ruling is brushed off as old news, because רב הושעיא already explained it in בבל. The גמרא then turns to the line in the כתובה promising support for daughters. רב and לוי word its endpoint differently, and the גמרא narrows their argument to one case: a girl who is betrothed (ארוסה) but not yet grown. That argument matches an older one among תנאים, and the meaning of רב יוסף's wording 'until they become' is left as תיקו. Next, רב חסדא and רב יוסף argue from logic about whether a betrothed orphan gets food from her father's estate. The גמרא records two versions of who said which reason. A memory aid then lists a series of questions about different women. רב ששת proves from a ברייתא that the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה disagree about a girl who refused her marriage (ממאנת). ריש לקיש's question about the daughter of a יבמה ends in תיקו, and רבי אלעזר begins a question about the daughter of a שניה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The reported ruling is not news
steps.stepSummary: Someone is told that the ruling he brought is not new, because רב הושעיא already explained it in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Thanks for nothing, your favor is thrown on the thorns. רב הושעיא already explained this teaching of yours back in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the previous discussion. It brushes off a report of a ruling, saying it adds nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself is not being rejected. What is rejected is the idea that the report is a new discovery. Since רב הושעיא already taught the same thing in בבל, the people of בבל do not owe the messenger thanks.

keyTerms.meaning: Your favor is taken (a sarcastic opening)
Thrown on the thorns, meaning it is worthless to us
He explained it
A teaching or ruling

phrases.english: Your favor is taken
and thrown on the thorns;
phrases.notes: A saying that means: we don't owe you any thanks for this news.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya already explained
this teaching of yours in Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion from before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the report is new. The ruling itself is accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teaching was already known in בבל through רב הושעיא.

steps.title: Two versions of the daughters' support clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the כתובה line about daughters. רב says they are supported until they are taken by men, and לוי says until they become grown women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the משנה: 'Female daughters you will have from me' will be supported from my property. רב's version says: 'until they are taken by men.' לוי's version says: 'until they become grown women.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It shows two different wordings of the כתובה clause about supporting daughters after the father dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ties the end of support to the girl being 'taken' by a husband. לוי ties it to her age, when she becomes a בוגרת. These two endpoints are not the same, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Female children, daughters
Teaches, reads the text as
They are taken by men (as wives)
They become grown women (בוגרות)

phrases.english: Female children that you will have
phrases.notes: This quotes the כתובה line from the משנה.

phrases.english: from me, etc.
Rav teaches: "until they are taken by men,"
and Levi teaches: "until they become grown women."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: support lasts until the daughters are taken by men. לוי: support lasts until they become grown women.

steps.title: Both versions look impossible
steps.stepSummary: Read literally, רב would give support even to a grown woman, and לוי would give support even to a married woman. Both seem wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב, does she still get support even after she is grown up?! And according to לוי, does she still get support even after she is married?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks both versions. Each one, read word for word, leads to a result that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only marriage ends support, as רב says, then an unmarried grown woman would still be supported. If only age ends support, as לוי says, then a young married girl would still be supported by her father's estate. Neither result makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
She became a grown woman
She got married

phrases.english: According to Rav, even though she has grown up?!
And according to Levi, even though she has married?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal meaning of both versions from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal wording of both רב's and לוי's versions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each version leaves out the other endpoint, so each leads to an unreasonable result.

steps.title: They only argue about a betrothed girl
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that growing up or marrying ends support. The only argument is about a girl who is betrothed but not yet grown.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if she grew up and didn't marry, or married and didn't grow up, everyone agrees her support ends. They only argue about a girl who is betrothed (ארוסה) and has not yet grown up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by shrinking the argument down to one case: the ארוסה who is not yet a בוגרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב and לוי accept both endpoints, so the impossible results from step 3 disappear. For רב, being 'taken' already happens at betrothal, so an ארוסה loses support. For לוי, only growing up or full marriage ends support, so an ארוסה keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Where they do disagree
A betrothed girl, after אירוסין but before נישואין

steps.confusionAlert: Betrothal (אירוסין) is a real, binding stage of marriage, but the bride has not yet moved in with her husband (נישואין). The whole argument depends on keeping these two stages apart.

phrases.english: Rather: if she grew up and did not marry,
or married and did not grow up,
everyone agrees.
phrases.notes: In both of these cases, everyone agrees her support has ended.

phrases.english: Where they disagree
is about a betrothed girl who has not grown up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: both endpoints are agreed on, and the argument is limited to one case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and לוי each have only one endpoint for support.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both accept both endpoints. They argue only about an ארוסה who is not yet grown.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the exact point of the argument for everything that follows.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: לוי's own ברייתא mentions both growing up and the time for full marriage, which supports the idea that he accepts both endpoints.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so לוי taught in his ברייתא: 'Until they become grown women and the time comes for them to be married.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from לוי's own collection of teachings, which mentions both endpoints.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'marriage' means full marriage (נישואין), not betrothal. That fits the claim that, for לוי, an ארוסה is still supported.

keyTerms.meaning: And so he taught (support from a source)
His ברייתא, his collection of teachings
Their time arrives

phrases.english: And so Levi taught in his collection of teachings:
"Until they become grown women
and the time arrives for them to be married."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That לוי accepts both growing up and full marriage as endpoints.

steps.title: Does she need both conditions?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's wording sounds like both conditions are needed before support ends, which makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two conditions? Does she really need both before support ends?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the word 'and' in לוי's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'grown up AND the time for marriage' would mean support continues until both have happened. But either one alone should be enough to end it.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (both conditions?)

phrases.english: Two?
phrases.notes: Meaning: must both conditions happen before her support stops?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the source quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Requiring both conditions would wrongly keep a grown woman or a married girl on support.

steps.title: Read it as either one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means either condition ends support: growing up or reaching the time of marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: either they become grown women, or their time arrives to be married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading by changing 'and' into 'or.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא matches step 4 exactly. Each endpoint works on its own, and betrothal alone does not end support for לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Either… or
To be married (full marriage)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: betrothal ends a daughter's support. לוי: only growing up or full marriage ends it, so an ארוסה is still supported.

phrases.english: Rather: either they become grown women
or their time arrives to be married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.

steps.title: The same argument among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: An earlier argument among תנאים matches רב and לוי: the first view says support lasts until betrothal, and רבי אלעזר says until she grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument among תנאים: Until when is a daughter supported? Until she is betrothed. In the name of רבי אלעזר they said: until she becomes a grown woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the רב and לוי argument already existed in an older argument among תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view, 'until she is betrothed,' matches רב. רבי אלעזר's view, 'until she grows up,' matches לוי, because an ארוסה would still be supported. So each אמורא has a תנא to lean on.

keyTerms.meaning: Like an argument among תנאים
Is supported (given food and needs)
That she becomes betrothed

phrases.english: It is like an argument among Tannaim:
Until when is a daughter supported?
Until she is betrothed.
In the name of Rabbi Elazar they said:
Until she becomes a grown woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the settled argument from steps 4 to 7 to an older argument among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the רב and לוי argument already appears among the תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the first view and the view of רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: רב יוסף's version: 'until they become'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף taught a third wording, 'until they become,' which leaves out what they become.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught the wording: 'until they become (someone's).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third version of the clause. Its unclear meaning sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'become' is a term for marriage, but it does not say which stage. That gap is what the next step asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: They become (someone's wife)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught: "until they become."
phrases.notes: Literally just 'until they become,' meaning become a man's wife. It doesn't say at which stage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third version alongside רב and לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daughters are supported 'until they become' someone's wife.

steps.title: Betrothal or full marriage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב יוסף's 'becoming' means betrothal or full marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: does 'becoming' mean becoming betrothed (אירוסין), or becoming fully married (נישואין)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב יוסף's wording means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it means אירוסין, his version matches רב. If it means נישואין, it matches לוי. So the question decides which side רב יוסף's version supports.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Becoming (a wife)
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Full marriage, the second stage

phrases.english: A question was asked:
Does it mean becoming betrothed,
or becoming married?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unclear wording in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'becoming' in רב יוסף's version means אירוסין or נישואין.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, and the question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know whether רב יוסף's version sides with רב or with לוי. The argument about the ארוסה remains open as far as his wording goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question is left unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: The only argument is about an ארוסה who is not yet grown. רב and the first תנא say her support ends, and לוי and רבי אלעזר say it continues. רב יוסף's wording 'until they become' is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question from step 10 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The meaning of רב יוסף's wording stays unresolved.

steps.title: Does a betrothed orphan girl get food from the estate?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks רב יוסף whether he heard from רב יהודה if an אֲרוּסָה gets מזונות from her father's estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רב יוסף: Did you hear from רב יהודה whether a betrothed girl gets food, or doesn't get food?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks a new practical question: once an orphan girl is betrothed, do her brothers still have to feed her from their father's estate?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that a daughter is fed from the estate until a certain point. Now the question is about a girl who is betrothed but not yet married. Does betrothal stop the estate's duty, since she now has a husband-to-be? רב חסדא hopes רב יוסף has a tradition from רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman, after קידושין but before full marriage (נישואין)
Food and support
Did you hear? A request for a received tradition

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Have you heard from Rav Yehuda
whether a betrothed girl has food,
phrases.notes: He means an orphan girl being fed from her father's estate, which now belongs to her brothers.

phrases.english: or she does not have food?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question after the תיקו, still on the topic of a daughter's support.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether betrothal ends an orphan girl's right to food from her father's estate.

steps.title: רב יוסף: no tradition, but logic says she gets no food
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף has no tradition. By logic she gets no food from the estate, because the ארוס doesn't want her lowered, so he will feed her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not hear anything, but by logic she does not get food. Since he betrothed her, he is not happy that she should be lowered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף admits he has no tradition from רב יהודה. He answers from logic: the betrothed girl does not get food from the estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is about what the ארוס wants. Once she is his betrothed, he would be embarrassed to have her begging her brothers for food, so he will support her himself. That means the estate doesn't need to.

keyTerms.meaning: From hearing: a tradition received from a teacher
From logic, reasoning on your own
That she be lowered or cheapened

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשְׁמָע לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: as for hearing, I have not heard,
but by logic she does not have food:
since he betrothed her,
phrases.notes: "He" is the man who betrothed her, not her brothers.

phrases.english: he is not happy that she be lowered.
phrases.notes: Literally "that she go cheap": having to ask her brothers for food would make her look lowly.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁמָע לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי, אֶלָּא מִסְּבָרָא לֵית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's question using logic, since there is no tradition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She gets no food from the estate, because the ארוס will feed her to protect her dignity.

steps.title: רב חסדא: logic says the opposite, she does get food
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא argues that by logic she does get food from the estate, because the ארוס isn't sure of her and won't spend money for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you did not hear it, then by logic she does get food. Since he is not sure of her, he will not throw away money for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rejects רב יוסף's reasoning and offers an opposite logic: the betrothed girl still gets food from the estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both look at the ארוס, but they read him differently. רב חסדא says a betrothed man isn't certain the marriage will happen, so he won't spend money on her yet. Since he won't feed her, the estate must keep feeding her.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not sure about her, that the marriage will go through
He won't throw money away for nothing

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם מִשְׁמָע לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: if you have not heard it,
by logic she has food.
Since he is not sure about her,
phrases.notes: He doesn't know yet whether they will actually end up married.

phrases.english: he will not throw away money for nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם מִשְׁמָע לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ, מִסְּבָרָא אִית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רב יוסף's logic with an opposite logic.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יוסף's conclusion that a betrothed girl gets no food.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the ארוס will pay for her, but a man unsure of the marriage won't spend money on her.

steps.title: Second version: רב יוסף says she does get food
steps.stepSummary: In a second version (איכא דאמרי), רב יוסף is the one who argues she gets food, because the ארוס won't spend money when he is unsure of her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: He said to him: I did not hear anything, but by logic she gets food. Since he is not sure of her, he will not throw away money for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the same conversation, with the two arguments switched. Here רב יוסף answers that she does get food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two arguments stay the same, but the speakers trade places. In this version רב יוסף uses the reasoning that the ארוס, unsure about the marriage, won't pay for her, so the estate must.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: a second version of the discussion

steps.confusionAlert: The two arguments did not change. Only who said which one flipped. Don't mix up the reasons; just track which speaker holds each one in each version.

phrases.english: And some say: he said to him:
phrases.notes: Here "he" is רב יוסף answering רב חסדא's question.

phrases.english: as for hearing, I have not heard,
by logic she has food —
since he is not sure about her,
he will not throw away money for nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the conversation in a second version, with רב יוסף now taking the opposite side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She gets food from the estate, because the ארוס won't pay while unsure of the marriage.

steps.title: Second version: רב חסדא says she gets no food
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, רב חסדא answers that by logic she gets no food, since the ארוס doesn't want her lowered and will feed her himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you did not hear it, then by logic she does not get food. Since he betrothed her, he is not happy that she should be lowered.
steps.whatsHappening: In the second version, רב חסדא rejects רב יוסף's view using the dignity reasoning: the betrothed girl does not get food from the estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of steps 13–14. The question stays open: either the ארוס feeds her out of concern for her honor, or he holds back his money because he is unsure of the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he betrothed her

steps.whatToRemember: Two logical arguments, with no tradition to settle them. (1) The ארוס cares about her honor, so he will feed her, and she gets nothing from the estate. (2) The ארוס is unsure of the marriage and won't spend money, so the estate feeds her. The two versions differ only in who said which.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי מִשְׁמָע לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: if you have not heard it,
by logic she does not have food.
Since he betrothed her,
he is not happy that she be lowered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשְׁמָע לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ, מִסְּבָרָא לֵית לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second-version answer of רב יוסף with the opposite logic.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the view that a betrothed girl gets food from the estate.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that the ארוס, out of concern for her honor, will support her himself.

steps.title: Memory aid for the next set of questions
steps.stepSummary: A סימן lists the חכמים (שק זרף) and the five cases (refusing girl, יבמה, שניה, betrothed, and raped woman) of the questions that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory aid for the men: שק זרף. She refused, a יבמה, a secondary relative (שניה), a betrothed woman, and a raped woman.
steps.whatsHappening: This line asks no question and gives no answer. It sets up the next section with a memory aid for the חכמים who will be quoted and the cases they will discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters שק זרף stand for one letter from each חכם's name. The list of cases tells us the coming questions are about whether different kinds of women get some right connected to the כתובה. The details come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid to keep a list in order
Of the men, meaning the חכמים who will speak
She refused: a girl married off as a minor who leaves the marriage by מיאון
A widow waiting for or married to her late husband's brother
A woman forbidden to him only by rabbinic law (שניות לעריות)
A woman who was raped

phrases.english: A memory aid for the men: Sh-K Z-R-F.
phrases.notes: Each letter hints at a name: רב ששת, ריש לקיש, רבי אלעזר, רבא, רב פפא.

phrases.english: She refused, and a yevama, a secondary relative,
a betrothed woman, and a raped woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ארוסה discussion and introduces a new series of questions with a memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; a memory aid listing the speakers and the five cases discussed next.

steps.title: Does a girl who refused her marriage still get food?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב ששת whether a ממאנת is still fed from her father's estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: a girl who refused her marriage, does she get food, or doesn't she?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first case from the סימן. The חכמים ask רב ששת whether a girl who did מיאון still gets food from her father's estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממאנת was a young orphan girl who was married off and then refused the marriage, which cancels it. A daughter normally gets food from her father's estate until she marries. The question is whether her marriage counts and ended her right to food, or whether the refusal wipes it out as if she was never married.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who refused (did מִיאוּן) a marriage arranged for her while she was a minor
Food and support, here from her late father's estate
They asked him (a question was put to a rabbi)

phrases.english: They asked of רב ששת:
A girl who refused, does she have food,
phrases.notes: This is a young orphan girl who was married off by her brothers or mother and then refused the husband.

phrases.english: or does she not have food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the first case listed in the סימן of step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a ממאנת keeps her right to food from her father's estate.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא about women back in their father's house
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the answer is in a ברייתא where the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה discuss food for women in their father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: You learned it in a ברייתא. A widow in her father's house, a divorcée in her father's house, and a woman waiting for her יבם in her father's house all get food. רבי יהודה says: if she is still in her father's house she gets food; if she is not in her father's house she does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers by pointing to a ברייתא. He is setting up a proof that he will explain in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא lists women who are back in their father's house and says they get food. רבי יהודה seems to add a condition about being in the father's house. On the surface, the two opinions sound almost the same, and that is what the next step points out.

keyTerms.meaning: You have already learned it (in a ברייתא)
A widow waiting for her husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה
In her father's house

phrases.english: רב ששת said to them: you learned it:
A widow in her father's house,
and a divorcée in her father's house,
and a woman waiting for her יבם in her father's house —
she has food.
רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹדָהּ בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ — יֵשׁ לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: If she is still in her father's house, she has food,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ — אֵין לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת.
phrases.english: if she is not in her father's house, she has no food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is found in a ברייתא; the proof is explained in the next step.

steps.title: The argument in the ברייתא must be about a ממאנת
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה seems to say the same as the תנא קמא, their real argument must be about a ממאנת: the תנא קמא says she gets food, רבי יהודה says she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבי יהודה saying the same thing as the תנא קמא?! Rather, isn't it that they argue about a girl who refused? The תנא קמא holds she gets food, and רבי יהודה holds she does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains his proof. Because the two opinions look the same, they must disagree about a ממאנת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two opinions in a ברייתא cannot be saying exactly the same thing, so there must be a case where they differ. רב ששת says that case is the ממאנת. The תנא קמא gives her food, since her marriage is undone, and רבי יהודה does not, since she already left her father's house in marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
Rather, isn't it that... (introduces the only possible explanation)
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The question about a ממאנת is a מחלוקת in the ברייתא: the תנא קמא says she gets food, and רבי יהודה says she does not.
steps.confusionAlert: The line 'is רבי יהודה the same as the תנא קמא?!' is not a real question waiting for a yes. It shows that they must disagree somewhere, and that somewhere is the ממאנת.

phrases.english: Is רבי יהודה the same as the first תנא?!
Rather, isn't it that a girl who refused is the difference between them,
that the first תנא holds she has food,
and רבי יהודה holds she does not have food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a ממאנת gets food from her father's estate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה, which must disagree about a ממאנת because otherwise their opinions would be the same.

steps.title: Does the daughter of a יבמה get food?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks whether the daughter born to a יבמה gets food.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked: the daughter of a יבמה, does she get food or doesn't she?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second case in the סימן. ריש לקיש asks about a daughter born from a יבום marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה is a widow who married her late husband's brother. If they had a daughter and he then died, the question is whether this daughter gets food from his estate like any other daughter. The next step lays out both sides of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question with no clear answer yet)
The daughter of a woman who married her יבם

phrases.english: ריש לקיש asked:
The daughter of a יבמה, does she have food
phrases.notes: He means a daughter born after the יבמה married her יבם, and the question is about food from his estate.

phrases.english: or does she not have food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first case in the סימן (ממאנת) to the second case (יבמה).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a daughter from a יבום marriage gets food from her father's estate.

steps.title: The two sides of the question about the יבמה's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out both sides of ריש לקיש's question. Maybe the daughter gets no food, since the mother's כתובה is owed by the first husband. Or maybe she does, since the Rabbis made the יבם back up the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master taught that a יבמה's כתובה is paid from her first husband's property, maybe the daughter has no right to food from the יבם. Or perhaps, since the Rabbis arranged that if the first husband's property is not enough, the כתובה is paid from the second husband's, the daughter does have a right to food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining why ריש לקיש's question from Step 21 is a real question. It shows the reasoning on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daughter's right to food comes from her mother's כתובה. Side one says the יבמה's כתובה belongs to the first husband, so the יבם's estate owes the daughter nothing. Side two says the Rabbis made the יבם's property a backup for the כתובה, so the כתובה is partly tied to him and the daughter should be fed from his estate.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract that promises the wife money, and also gives her daughters food after the father dies
The property of her first husband, the one who died
Or perhaps. It brings in the second side of a question
The Rabbis made a rule (a תקנה)
She does not have / she does have

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the כתובה is first paid from the first husband's property. They only disagree about whether the Rabbis' backup from the יבם is enough to tie the daughter's food to the יבם.

phrases.english: Since the Master said
her marriage contract is paid from the property of her first husband,
phrases.notes: "Her" means the יבמה, the mother. The first husband is the one who died without children.

phrases.english: she does not have [food],
phrases.notes: Now "she" means the daughter. The question is whether the יבם's estate must feed her.

phrases.english: or perhaps:
since if she does not have enough from the first,
the Rabbis enacted for her payment from the second,
she does have [food]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of ריש לקיש's question from Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the daughter of a יבמה fed from the יבם's estate, given that her mother's כתובה comes mainly from the first husband but is backed up by the יבם?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question about the יבמה's daughter is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle the question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means neither side was proven. The question about the יבמה's daughter stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question is left without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a יבמה's daughter is fed from the יבם's estate is left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from Steps 21 and 22 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about the daughter of a יבמה remains unresolved.

steps.title: Does a daughter from a שניה get food?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether a daughter born from a marriage forbidden only by the Rabbis (a שניה) gets food from her father's estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: does the daughter of a שניה get food, or does she not get food?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. This is the third case listed in the סימן from Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis punish a woman married in a שניה relationship by taking away her כתובה. Since a daughter's food comes from the כתובה rules, רבי אלעזר asks whether the daughter loses her food too, or whether the punishment applies only to the mother.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative the Rabbis forbade a man to marry, even though the תורה allows it
Food or support paid from the father's estate
He asked. It opens a question the גמרא wants to explore

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
the daughter of a secondary relative,
phrases.notes: A שניה is a relative forbidden only by the Rabbis. The mother loses her כתובה as a penalty.

phrases.english: does she have food,
or does she not have food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the סימן, after the יבמה question ended with תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the Rabbis' penalty on a שניה, taking away her כתובה, also take away her daughter's right to food?
